source.description: Base failure rates (λb) for electronic part types from the part stress models of the U.S. military's reliability prediction handbook, with each section's environment factors (πE) for its 14 use environments, from ground, benign to cannon, launch.
caveats: A handbook prediction model, not failures counted in service: never mix it with field data.

Reliafy uses the base failure rate × the environment factor only. The handbook's other factors (temperature, electrical stress, quality and more) aren't applied: each record names them, and real rates depend on them. Quality alone can move a rate by a factor of 10 or more.
The models were last revised in 1995 and describe parts of that era; newer parts are often more reliable than the handbook predicts.
The handbook is guidance for comparing designs early, not a measure of how your equipment will fail.

skipped.what: Microcircuits (gate arrays, memories, VHSIC, GaAs, hybrids, SAW, bubble memories)
skipped.reason: The model adds a die term and a package term (C1 πT + C2 πE), each from the device's complexity and package: there is no one base failure rate per part type.

skipped.what: Diodes, low frequency: power rectifier with high voltage stacks
skipped.reason: The base rate is per junction (.0050 per junction): it needs the number of junctions.

skipped.what: Transistors, high frequency (low noise bipolar, high power bipolar, GaAs FET, Si FET)
skipped.reason: The base rate is a formula of frequency and output power (or a table of them), not one number per type.
The base rate is a formula of the number of characters and whether a logic chip is included.
The base rate depends on the material and on optical power and current.

skipped.what: Tubes (including travelling wave tubes and magnetrons)
skipped.reason: Not imported in this release: the base rates depend on tube type, power and frequency, and few designs use tubes now.
The base rates depend on the laser's construction, power and pumping.
A life model for bearings and windings (characteristic lives by temperature), with no environment factor: not a constant base rate.
The base rate is a formula of the frame temperature.
The base rate depends on the ambient temperature (.0059 at 25 °C to .031 at 125 °C for a 125 °C rated relay): no one number per type.

skipped.what: Interconnection assemblies with plated through holes
skipped.reason: The base rate is per plated through hole, weighted by the number of circuit planes: it needs the board's hole counts.
A wear-out model in thermal cycles, not a constant base rate.
The base rate is a formula of frequency (.013 f^0.23).
The base rate is a formula of rated voltage (.074 Vr^1.29).
The rate is per kilometre of fibre, a unit the library doesn't convert.
The handbook refers these to the resistor model (style RD).

skipped.what: Microwave fixed elements (directional couplers, fixed stubs and cavities)
skipped.reason: The handbook gives their rate as negligible, not a number.

skipped.what: Terminations (thin or thick film loads in stripline and thin film circuits)
skipped.reason: Given as 0.030 × πE without saying which environment table applies.

skipped.what: Parts count method (generic failure rates by environment)
skipped.reason: A different method, for early estimates: not imported in this release.
